items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: there was Bix and Murray and [Howdy] Quicksell (phonetic) and Bill Rank. And Trumbauer. They had a good jazz band there

ctx.x: can gather, he left the Wolverines because the Harman guys who told me about it, they played opposite the Wolverines in the Cinderella, and they told me that most of the time Jimmy McPartland had kind of taken his place for about five months or so, a six month engagement something like that.

So that's -- that was hearing, that was my experience hearing him, but here now it was a more mature Bix, and Trumbauer for that matter, and the band was -- it was good, they were on a road trip. The Goldkette band had been split up from out of the Greystone band that spring. They sent part of it which they called the waltz band and they played some job there and then they took the jazz group, took it down to a place called Hudson Lake and there was Bix and Murray and [Howdy] Quicksell (phonetic) and Bill Rank.…

Now, then, in August they brought them all together again because they were going to go back in to the Greystone. Whether the Greystone closed for the summer or what they did, that summer anyway, I don't know, but the band was taken out and split up. Now, they were putting them together so they booked them on a road trip and one of their stops was the Cinderella Ballroom in Wilkes Barre. So we went into hear them.
